assessment: Sphingomyelin synthase 2 (SMS2) is an enzyme located in the Golgi apparatus and the plasma membrane (PM) that mediates the synthesis of sphingomyelin (SM), a critical lipid in the PM. Mutations in SMS2 underlie a rare genetic disorder of bone formation. This useful study shows that the disease mutations cause retention of SMS2 in the ER, producing SM in the wrong place and leading to a disrupted SM/cholesterol gradient in the membranes of the secretory pathway. In addition to highlighting the roles of lipid gradients in cellular signaling pathways, this study also provides cell biologists with new tools to examine lipid localization in cells.
